data.name: Skim Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Skim milk powder (SMP) prices increased at both ends of the range this reporting period, with gains at the lower end outpacing those at the upper end. Processor prices were up from both last month and year-ago levels, with a 54 percent improvement year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes increased last week compared to the week prior, with double the lots traded. SMP futures strengthened across all contract periods, increasing by as much as 2.5 percent for March. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative maintained its projected total SMP offerings for the next 12 months. September export volumes were up 31 percent YoY, bringing year-to-date growth to 9 percent. Strong gains were driven by a 62 percent increase in shipments to Asia excluding China and a 201 percent jump in purchases from Australia/Oceania. Meanwhile, exports to China and the Middle East declined by 16 percent and 54 percent, respectively.

SMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 415 increased across all offered contract periods, led by January, which was up 3.7 percent. No product was offered for April or May. January and February accounted for 80 percent of total sales. Total volume sold was similar to Event 414 and slightly above year-earlier levels. North Asia was the top buyer, purchasing 39 percent of the total volume, which was the same as the previous event but down from 51 percent a year ago. Southeast Asia/Oceania followed with 35 percent. The SMP average price is 60 percent higher YoY and has traded at a premium to whole milk powder the last several events.

data.name: Whole Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Whole milk powder (WMP) prices moved higher across the full price range, with the largest gain at the top this reporting period. Processor prices increased from last month and are 5 percent higher than year-ago levels. Futures trading volumes increased 21 percent last week compared to the week prior. WMP futures strengthened for all contract periods, increasing by as much as 1.2 percent for November. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative reported that the forecast total offer volume for WMP over the next 12 months remains unchanged. September export volumes increased 21 percent year-over-year (YoY), lifting year-to-date growth to 12 percent. Growth was driven by a 208 percent surge in shipments to North Africa, a 32 percent increase in exports to Asia excluding China, and higher volumes to the Middle East, North America, and South America. These gains more than offset a 19 percent decline in shipments to China.

WMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 415 increased across all contract periods offered and the average WMP reached its highest level since August 2025. The January contract saw the largest increase, up 6.7 percent. No product was offered for April or May. January and February accounted for 76 percent of total sales. Sales volumes were lower than both Event 414 and year-earlier levels. North Asia was the top buyer, purchasing 73 percent of the volume, up from 54 percent at the previous auction and up from 57 percent a year ago. The Middle East bought 12 percent of the volume, followed by Southeast Asia/Oceania at 10 percent. WMP has traded at a discount to skim milk powder over the past several events, adding further upward pressure to prices.

data.name: Cheddar Cheese
data.narrative:
Cheddar cheese prices narrowed this reporting period, strengthening considerably at the bottom of the range while easing at the top. Processor prices were higher than the previous month but remain 15 percent below year-ago levels. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative maintained its projected total cheddar offerings for the next 12 months. September export volumes increased 16 percent year-over-year (YoY), driven by stronger shipments to Asian markets outside of China. Growing global demand for whey proteins continues to support higher cheese production, while rising inventories and export volumes are placing downward pressure on cheddar prices.

At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 415, cheddar prices were mostly higher for all contract periods offered, with the lone exception of November. The January contract recorded the largest increase, rising 12 percent. No cheddar was offered for the May contract at this event. January and February accounted for 66 percent of all cheddar sales. Sales volumes were similar to Event 414 and year-ago levels. Africa led purchasing, followed by the Middle East.

data.name: Butter
data.narrative: Butter prices decreased at both ends of the range, with the biggest drop at the bottom this reporting period. Processor prices decreased compared to last month and remain down 30 percent year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes were 13 percent lower last week compared to the week prior. Last week's butter futures were steady for November; weaker for December, February, and March; and stronger for January and April. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative maintained its projected total butter offerings for the next 12 months. September export volumes climbed 23 percent YoY, bringing year-to-date growth to 13 percent, as shipments to China, Oceania, the Middle East, and Asia strengthened. At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 415, butter prices were mostly lower, with January losing the most ground, down 6.1 percent. No butter was offered for April or May. January and February accounted for 85 percent of total sales. Butter volume sold increased compared to Event 414 and year-ago levels. North Asia led purchasing with 78 percent, followed by the Middle East and Southeast Asia/Oceania. Offer volumes increased 10 percent for this event, adding downward pressure to prices. Cream supplies remain plentiful and trade data points to abundant global butter supplies, supported by strong production growth in Europe, the United States, Argentina, and New Zealand.
